To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) posterior parahippopampal cortex, a region of the medial temporal lobe, preferentially activated to indoor scenes compared to outdoor scenes; (2) this region is likely involved in local space perception; (3) retrosplenial cortex also preferentially activated to real-world scenes compared with faces but did not differ between indoor and outdoor scenes.
(i) posterior parahippicampal place area preferentially activates to indoor scenes, and (ii) retrosplenial cortex preferentially activates to scenes compared to faces.
posterior parahipppocampal cortex but not retrosplenial cortex preferentially activates to indoor scenes compared to outdoor scenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying the representation of real world scenes in the human brain.
the neural mechanisms of scene analysis.
the question of what are the neural mechanisms that underlie the perception of real-world scenes, and the neural mechanisms that distinguish the perception of different types of real-world scenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the posterior parahippicampal cortex, which has previously been implicated in scene processing, is functionally specialized to process indoor scenes.
the parahippocampus is involved in processing of local space, whereas the retrosplenial cortex is involved in processing spatial relations.

there are two distinct cortical systems for processing scenes, with posterior parahippicampal cortex being involved in the processing of indoor space and retrosplenial area involved in the processing and memory for large scale outdoor space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
posterior parahipppocampal cortex (PPA), including parahippcampal place area (PPA), is functional in processing of local space.
posterior parahipocampus processes the local space and the retrosplenial cortex processes the global space.
posterior parahipppocampal cortex preferentially activates to scenes with a local spatial structure, while retrosplenial cortex is more broadly involved in scene processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two scene-selective areas, posterior parhippocampal and retrosplenial cortices, have distinct functional properties.
there are different sub-regions of posterior parahippicampal cortex that are sensitive to different aspects of the visual scene.

the posterior parahippopampal cortex, which has previously been shown to preferentially process real-world scenes, also shows greater activation to indoor than outdoor scenes, which is consistent with its role in processing local space and spatial layout.
